hero.source_note: Named/distinctive character — source from Creative Fabrica or TPT clip art; look for red chick with book or bedtime setting

ambiguous.reason: The chicken literally jumps into the story text on the page — the action of interrupting is the core meaning; use interrupt icon if available, otherwise jumping-in gesture

notes: Core vocabulary already covers several key concepts for this book: 'stop' (Papa tells chicken to stop interrupting), 'listen', 'sleep', 'interrupt' are in aac_extras; 'book', 'bed', 'father', 'chicken', 'night', 'fairy tale', 'witch', 'wolf' are in activity_images. The 11 fringe words therefore focus on gaps: the repeated action of jumping into stories, the bedtime darkness, the fairy-tale settings (forest, house), the character being little and red, tiredness (Papa grows tired), trying (Papa tries to read), and the story concept itself. 'Again' is included because Papa repeatedly attempts to read stories — it is a high-frequency communicative concept for this book even though it appears in some core sets; confirm it is absent from this board's fixed core rows before finalising. The fairy-tale characters (Hansel & Gretel, Chicken Little) are referenced but wolf and witch are already in activity_images, so no additional character sourcing is needed beyond the hero.
